Architectural overview

Problem & architectural thesis

Retail analytics, staffing, and pricing studies often lack repeatable transaction datasets tied to physical store layouts and deterministic controls. PriceRiot pairs a POS CSV parameter-extraction ETL with a headless C++17 discrete-event agent engine, dynamic SKU pricing, multi-run sweeps, and out-of-sample evaluation.

Control flow

  1. Propose / IngestPOS CSV ETL, Pricing & YAML Spec

    Cleans POS transaction exports, maps SKUs, fits arrival parameters out-of-sample, and configures YAML layouts, staffing, and SKU price multipliers.

  3. Deterministic CoreC++17 Engine, Elasticity & Sweeps

    Runs deterministic A* navmesh agents with price-elasticity acceptance across typed pybind11 bindings, multi-day TemporalScheduler, and /api/sweeps.

  5. Commit / VerifyCalibrated Logs, Dashboards & Eval

    Persists runs/sweeps to SQLite, exports CSVs to FastAPI/Vue 3 and Streamlit, and scores held-out calibration and elasticity invariants.

Key tradeoff & failure mode

Held-out synthetic POS calibration matched 6 schedule-aligned Mon-Sat open days within -3.22% transactions and +4.03% revenue (0.0325 intraday TVD), and controlled price markups produced monotonic demand drops (-0.414 to -0.941 arc elasticity) with stable control SKUs. Because extract_params() transfers only spawn_interval_seconds, SKU top-10 overlap stayed at 38% and a Sunday schedule mismatch widened 7-day transaction error to -15.23%; fit to real (non-synthetic) store data is not tested. Automated layout optimization (P3.9) and built-in ML (P4) are formally closed as out of scope for v1.

What it is

  • PriceRiot is a headless-capable C++17 retail-store simulation exposed to Python via pybind11: customer and worker agents pathfind (A* on a navmesh) through a YAML-defined store, respond to per-SKU dynamic pricing, and emit synthetic transaction records. #priceriot-engine
  • A POS ingestion pipeline cleans historical transaction CSVs, maps SKUs, and extracts simulation parameters (spawn interval and basket profile), which the webapp and temporal scheduler apply at run time. #priceriot-pos-etl
  • PriceRiot v1 was closed out with dynamic pricing elasticity hooks in C++, queued-run staffing updates (POST /api/runs/{id}/workers), a multi-run parameter-sweep engine and API (/api/sweeps), and a full-stack test suite (27 Python+C++ pytest tests and 16 Vue 3 Vitest tests). #priceriot-pricing-sweeps-tests
  • In a leakage-free 21-day to 7-day held-out calibration over synthetic Cowboy Market POS data (N=5 seeds), transferring only the fitted spawn interval (449.13s) matched 6 schedule-aligned Mon-Sat open days within -3.22% transactions and +4.03% revenue with 0.0325 intraday period TVD, while exposing uncalibrated SKU-mix limits (38% top-10 overlap) and a Sunday schedule mismatch (-15.23% across all 7 calendar days). #priceriot-calibration-holdout
  • In a controlled dynamic-pricing experiment via set_sku_price across 5 seeds (target SKUs 1-5 vs control SKUs 6-30), target demand declined monotonically from 130.0 units at 0.75x to 9.4 units at 3.00x (implied arc elasticity -0.414 to -0.941) while control-group volume stayed stable (364.2-390.8 units). #priceriot-pricing-elasticity

What was measured2 entries

MEASURED LINKED #priceriot-calibration-holdout as of 2026-11-25

In a leakage-free 21-day to 7-day held-out calibration over synthetic Cowboy Market POS data (N=5 seeds), transferring only the fitted spawn interval (449.13s) matched 6 schedule-aligned Mon-Sat open days within -3.22% transactions and +4.03% revenue with 0.0325 intraday period TVD, while exposing uncalibrated SKU-mix limits (38% top-10 overlap) and a Sunday schedule mismatch (-15.23% across all 7 calendar days).

Does not showFit to real (non-synthetic) store foot traffic or POS receipts: cowboy_pos.csv is synthetically generated. The SKU-mix and basket-size gaps reflect that extract_params() only transfers spawn_interval_seconds into the C++ engine.
